# 1. Full call chains into `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend`

The PCI PM entry point in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915` is `i915_pm_ops` (`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1713-1754`, an `i915_pci_driver`-style `dev_pm_ops`). Only two of its callbacks actually reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

| dev_pm_ops slot | Event | Chain |
|---|---|---|
| `.suspend = i915_pm_suspend` (L1719) | PMSG_SUSPEND (S3 / S0ix) | `PCI/ACPI PM core → i915_pm_suspend() → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)` |
| `.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend` (L1745) | PMSG_HIBERNATE (S4, before image write / after restore) | `S4 PM core → i915_pm_suspend() → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)` |

Chain detail (ground truth from source):

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)                     i915_driver.c:1392
  │  i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  │  if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF) → return 0  (switcheroo off)
  └─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                       i915_driver.c:1392→1103
          dev_priv  = to_i915(dev)
          display   = dev_priv->display
          ├─ disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm)
          ├─ intel_power_domains_disable(display)
          ├─ drm_client_dev_suspend(dev)
          ├─ drm_kms_helper_poll_disable(dev) / intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display)
          ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)   ← display suspend (see §3)
          ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv), intel_hpd_cancel_work(display)
          ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display), intel_encoder_suspend_all(display)
          ├─ intel_dpt_suspend(display); i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt)
          ├─ i9xx_display_sr_save(display)
          ├─ intel_opregion_suspend(display, PCI_D1|PCI_D3cold)
          ├─ dev_priv->suspend_count++; intel_dmc_suspend(display)
          ├─ enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(...); i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)
```

The *other* paths that also call `i915_drm_suspend` (not PCI PM callbacks, for completeness — `i915_drm_suspend` has exactly 3 direct callers in the graph):

```
.freeze = i915_pm_freeze                       i915_driver.c:1487 (PMSG_FREEZE/QUIESCE)
  └─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)  (when switch_power_state != DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
      then i915_gem_freeze(i915)

i915_switcheroo_set_state()                    i915_switcheroo.c
  └─► i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo()         i915_driver.c:1210
      ├─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
      ├─► i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
      └─► pci_save_state(pdev); pci_set_power_state(pdev, PCI_D3hot)
```

The remaining callbacks (`.suspend_late` → `i915_pm_suspend_late`, `.suspend_noirq` → `i915_pm_suspend_noirq`, `.poweroff_late/_noirq` → `i915_pm_poweroff_late/_noirq`) do **not** touch `i915_drm_suspend` — they only do the PCIe D-state / power-sequencing work (and `freeze_late` → `i915_pm_freeze_late` calls `i915_drm_suspend_late`, not `i915_drm_suspend`).

# 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`?

**None — because `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` does not exist in this tree.** A whole-tree symbol search for `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` returns 0 hits (same for `i915_runtime_suspend`); that name is from the ~4.x-5.x i915, before runtime PM was restructured into `intel_runtime_pm`.

In this kernel the roles are split and verified via call graphs:

- PCI PM (S3/S4) path: `i915_pm_suspend`/`i915_pm_freeze`/`i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo` → `i915_drm_suspend` + `i915_drm_suspend_late` (direct callers of `i915_drm_suspend_late`: `i915_pm_suspend_late`, `i915_pm_freeze_late`, `i915_pm_poweroff_late`, `i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo`) — none of them calls any `..._runtime_suspend` wrapper; they go straight to the PCI layer.
- Runtime PM (S0ix) path: `i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend` (i915_driver.c:1752), which is **mutually exclusive** with the PCI PM path — its callees are `intel_display_power_suspend`, `intel_gt_runtime_suspend`, `i915_gem_runtime_suspend`, `intel_uncore_suspend`, `intel_irq_suspend` etc. It never passes through `i915_drm_suspend` or `intel_display_driver_suspend`.

# 3. Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` down to display suspend

Note: in this tree the display-suspend function is **`intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *)`** (`display/intel_display_driver.c:684`) — the name `intel_display_suspend` no longer exists. Flow of the private data:

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
    i915 (struct drm_i915_private *) = kdev_to_i915(kdev)     ← container_of via to_drm_i915
    i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                              ← passes struct drm_device *

i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)                      i915_driver.c:1103
    dev_priv = to_i915(dev)        →  struct drm_i915_private * (container_of, i915_drv.h)
    display  = dev_priv->display   →  struct intel_display * (field of drm_i915_private)

        └─► intel_display_driver_suspend(display)             display/intel_display_driver.c:684
                display->drm                          ← reverse backlink to struct drm_device
                state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
                display->restore.modeset_state = state
                flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup)
                intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)

        (still using dev_priv directly for the non-display parts:)
    intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
    i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt)
    suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) → opregion PCI_D1 vs PCI_D3cold
    dev_priv->suspend_count++
    disable/enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm)
    i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)
```

So the object handed down is `dev_priv` (`drm_i915_private`) converted one level: `to_i915(dev)` recovers it from `drm_device`, then `dev_priv->display` extracts the `intel_display` sub-object, which is what `intel_display_driver_suspend` receives; the `display->drm` back-pointer is used inside it to reach the core DRM APIs (`drm_atomic_helper_suspend`). The `dev_priv`-specific operations (IRQ, GGTT, opregion, GEM drain) stay in `i915_drm_suspend` itself.
